correctness.rationale: For n>=3 and J!=0, diagonal collision-loss kernel is exactly the set of H0-eigenvectors with zero amplitudes at every |x,x>. Fourier total-momentum analysis proves that all nonresonant dark modes are swap antisymmetric; the sole even-n p=n/2 sector is a zero-energy n-dimensional flat space with one detected Fourier diagonal direction. The resulting orthogonal projector, rank and pair amplitudes follow algebraically for every n; the semigroup decay argument handles arbitrary positive unequal rates. Standalone integer projector identities and independent finite-field Krylov ranks agree for all n=3,...,10. Assumptions and proof limits are explicit.

originality.rationale: Read the principal quantum-walk dark-state paper (Krovi–Brun 2006), the two-walker meeting paper (Štefaňák et al. 2007), continuous-time two-particle periodic-walk paper (Qin et al. 2014), and the localized-loss Bose–Hubbard paper (Kepesidis–Hartmann 2012). These establish general dark space arguments, quantum statistics, interacting pair motion, and local one-body protection, respectively. None supplies the many-site collision-loss projector, the independent-of-rates arbitrary-state capture law, or the mod-four antipodal bosonic survival classification. Existing general spectral mechanisms and fermionic antisymmetry are credited rather than claimed new. An unindexed exact two-body loss/observability predecessor remains possible.

value.rationale: Permanent two-body collision loss is a natural observable distinct from transient meeting probabilities. The theorem gives a complete operator law for arbitrary quantum states and any positive site-dependent loss profile on every finite ring, isolates a sharp odd-versus-even bosonic protection transition, and predicts a further mod-four antipodal interference effect. The exact all-n projector is directly reusable for mixed states and wavepackets, rather than a routine isolated finite-case count. It does not claim quantitative finite-time decay rates.
